item.title: Who Was Missing From Every List? — Lincoln (1930) Capture–Recapture, Sekar & Deming Vital Registers, Hypergeometric Posteriors & Bayesian Model-Averaged Multiple-Systems Estimation in El Salvador (Hoover Green & Ball)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Teaching Pilot 115: Lincoln (1930) Duck-Band Capture–Recapture, Sekar & Deming (1949) Vital Registration Canvass, Hypergeometric Overlap Posteriors, Madigan & York List Dependence & Hoover Green–Ball El Salvador Civil War Multiple-Systems Estimation. ## Act I · Look for a name you have seen before

item.title: The Debt They Had to Kill — X-Ray Micro-CT Virtual Unwrapping of Sealed Old Assyrian Cuneiform Envelopes from Kanesh (Kt 93/k 144) & Five-Mina Silver Loan Cancellation
item.description: Ancient Human History of Language Episode 40: How micro-CT scanning and 3D surface segmentation read sealed Old Assyrian clay letter Kt 93/k 144 from Kanesh without breaking its envelope, revealing instructions to surrender and 'kill' a separate five-mina silver debt tablet (Michel et al. 2026).

item.title: The Red Ink That Left a Shadow — Synchrotron XRF/XRD Mapping of Tebtunis Temple Papyri, Hematite Strokes With Lead-Phosphate Coffee-Ring Halos & Roman Bronze Inkwell Corrosion
item.description: Synchrotron archaeometry of ancient Egyptian medical/ritual papyri (#39): Christiansen et al.'s (2020 PNAS) sub-micrometer XRF/XRD/FTIR mapping of 12 Tebtunis temple-library fragments showing hematite red-ocher pigment surrounded by sub-visible lead-phosphate/sulfate coffee-ring margins and lead palmitate, copper-bearing soot in Pathyris/Tebtunis black inks (2017), and Sibilia et al.'s (2021) Este Roman bronze inkwell distinguishing carbon-gum ink from container-corrosion cerussite (84% of Pb) and malachite.

item.title: The Water the City Kept — Tikal Maya Corriental Crystalline Quartz & Zeolite Filtration, Cinnabar Mercury & Cyanobacterial eDNA Across Urban Reservoirs
item.description: Ancient urban hydrology and geoarchaeology at Classic Maya Tikal (#32): Scarborough et al.'s (2012) reservoir excavation framework, Tankersley et al.'s (2020) discovery of imported volcanogenic clinoptilolite/mordenite zeolites and macrocrystalline quartz in Corriental sediments, Lentz et al.'s (2020) cinnabar-derived mercury and Planktothrix cyanobacterial eDNA in central palace reservoirs, and 2021 arboreal sediment eDNA.

item.title: The Glue That Kept the Stone — Neanderthal North Sea & Königsaue Birch-Bark Tar Adhesives, Condensation vs. Pit Distillation, Lap-Shear Mechanics & Biomarker Limits
item.description: Middle Paleolithic pyrotechnology and experimental archaeometry (#33): the Dutch North Sea Zandmotor Neanderthal tar-backed flint flake (Niekus et al. 2019), Kozowyk et al.'s (2017) experimental birch-bark tar yields across ash-mound, pit-roll, and raised-structure methods, Schmidt et al.'s (2021, 2023) lap-shear mechanical testing and FTIR/GC-MS comparison of the two Königsaue artifacts, and Kozowyk et al.'s (2023) biomarker equifinality limits.

item.title: The Spears the Lake Kept — Schöningen Waterlogged Spruce & Pine Weapons, Javelin Ballistic Trials, Double-Pointed Throwing Stick & 2025 Amino-Acid Geochronology
item.description: Pleistocene organic woodworking and experimental ballistics at Schöningen 13 II-4 (#34): Leder et al.'s (2024) 187-piece spruce/pine/larch woodworking Chaîne Opératoire and resharpening traces, Milks et al.'s (2019) trained javelin-athlete replica throws and (2023) double-pointed throwing-stick micro-wear analysis, and Hutson et al.'s (2025) Bithynia opercula amino-acid racemization ~200 ka MIS 7 chronology revision.

item.title: The Knots That Kept the Count — Locke's Base-10 Inka Khipu Proof, Incahuasi Storehouse Accounting, Collata Epistolary Cords & Human-Hair Isotope Provenance
item.description: Andean cord-keeping from decimal state accounting to material bioarchaeology (#35): L. Leland Locke's (1912) base-10 positional proof on museum khipus, Gary Urton's (2018) Incahuasi agricultural warehouse khipus with fixed subtraction/commission fractions, Sabine Hyland's (2017) San Juan de Collata colonial epistolary cords, and Hyland et al.'s (2025) carbon/nitrogen/sulfur stable-isotope dietary profiling of a human-hair khipu.

item.title: A Sentence on a Comb — Tel Lachish Canaanite Ivory Lice Comb Inscription, Microscopic Head-Louse Remains, Early Alphabetic Paleography & Barley Radiocarbon Context
item.description: Early alphabetic epigraphy and archaeological dating at Tel Lachish (#36): Vainstub et al.'s (2022) reflectance transformation imaging of 17 shallow Canaanite letters ('May this tusk root out the lice of the hair and the beard') alongside a preserved Pediculus humanus capitis nymph membrane between the comb teeth, Haring's early alphabetic script history, and Webster (2019) & Höflmayer (2021) AMS radiocarbon dating of stratified Lachish barley seeds.

item.title: The Sound Inside the Shell — Magdalenian Marsoulas Cave Charonia Seashell Horn, Cave Impulse-Response Archaeoacoustics, Chavín Pututus & Neolithic Shell Trumpets
item.description: Archaeoacoustics and prehistoric aerophone mechanics (#37): Fritz et al.'s (2021) CT and acoustic study of the modified Magdalenian Charonia lampas shell horn from Marsoulas Cave producing three near-harmonic pitches around C4–D#4, Kolar et al.'s (2012, 2022) in-situ architectural acoustics at Chavín de Huántar and Marsoulas Cave, and López-García et al.'s (2025) Catalonian Neolithic shell trumpets.

item.title: The Four Sealed Translations — The 1857 Royal Asiatic Society Blind Assyrian Decipherment Test (Rawlinson, Hincks, Fox Talbot, Oppert) vs. Modern ORACC Cuneiform
item.description: Epistemology of ancient script decipherment (#38): the May 1857 Royal Asiatic Society blind verification experiment comparing four sealed independent translations of the newly excavated Qalat Sherqat clay prism of Tiglath-Pileser I by Rawlinson, Hincks, Fox Talbot, and Oppert, Rassam's excavation record, polyvalent syllabic vs. logographic sign behavior, and line-by-line audit against the modern ORACC RIAo edition.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Enzyme That Changed the Fatty Acid Map — FADS1/FADS2 Haplotypes, Delta-5/Delta-6 Desaturase Cytochrome b5 Electron Transfer, [U-13C]ALA Conversion & Greenlandic Selection
item.description: From European lipidomic GWAS of phosphatidylcholine PC 36:4 across FADS1/FADS2 haplotypes A and D (Ameur et al. 2012) to front-end delta-6/delta-5 desaturase HPGG cytochrome b5 architecture, Gillingham et al. [U-13C]ALA tracer recovery in plasma [13C]EPA (3.77% vs. 0.89% at 48h), and Greenlandic Inuit vs. ancient European selection scans (Fumagalli 2015; Mathieson 2018, 2020).

item.title: The Shell With a Second Life — Marine Shell Personal Ornaments, Use-Wear Microscopy, Ochre Residue & Middle Stone Age Symbolic Exchange
item.description: Taphonomic and microscopic reconstruction of Paleolithic perforated shell ornaments: distinguishing natural marine predation and wave abrasion from human suspension wear, stringing facets, ochre residue, and long-distance inland transport.

item.title: The Scroll That Stayed Rolled — Virtual Unwrapping from En-Gedi's Metal-Bearing Ink (Seales 2016) to Herculaneum Carbon Ink (Parker 2019) & Complete Surface Reading of PHerc. 1667 & Philodemus's On Gods Book 8
item.description: X-ray micro-CT virtual unwrapping and machine-learned carbon-ink detection in carbonized ancient scrolls: Seales et al.'s (2016) reading of Leviticus inside the charred En-Gedi scroll, Parker et al.'s (2019) 3D voxel ink classification on Herculaneum fragment PHerc. Paris 2 Fr. 96, and Angelotti et al.'s (2026 preprint) end-to-end surface reconstruction of PHerc. 1667 and title identification of Philodemus's On Gods Book 8 in PHerc. 139.

item.title: The Paint Beneath the Stone — Uranium-Thorium Calcite Dating, Sulawesi & Iberian Cave Art Stratigraphy & Pleistocene Pigment Chemistry
item.description: Archaeometric dating and chemical characterization of Pleistocene cave art beneath carbonate speleothem crusts: laser-ablation U-Th minimum age constraints in Sulawesi and Iberia, ochre/manganese pigment recipes, and stratigraphic cross-sections.

item.title: A Jaw From the Missing Chapter — Paleoproteomics, Mandibular Morphology & Middle Pleistocene Hominin Lineages
item.description: Paleoanthropological and paleoproteomic investigation of a fossil hominin mandible where ancient DNA failed: enamel/dentine collagen peptide mass fingerprinting, morphometric geometry, and what a single bone can and cannot resolve.

item.title: The Islands Kept Their Words — Teouma Lapita Ancient Genomes in Vanuatu, Near-Complete Papuan Ancestry Turnover & Why Austronesian Oceanic Languages Persisted
item.description: Reconciling ancient genomics, Lapita dentate-stamped pottery, and historical linguistics in Remote Oceania: why 3,000-year-old Teouma individuals carried minimal Papuan ancestry, how subsequent migration transformed Vanuatu's gene pool without replacing its Austronesian Oceanic languages, and why pots, genes, and words move along distinct historical channels.

item.title: The Grave With Two Calendars — Repton Viking Charnel Deposit, Anglo-Saxon Silver Coin Hoard (873–874 CE) vs. Bone Collagen Radiocarbon & Marine Reservoir Correction
item.description: Archaeometric resolution of the Repton Viking Great Army charnel deposit: why five silver pennies in Grave 529 dated the burial to 873–874 CE while uncalibrated terrestrial bone collagen 14C dates appeared centuries older, and how Jarman et al. (2018) combined delta-13C/delta-15N dietary paleodiet reconstruction with marine reservoir correction (Heaton et al. 2020 Marine20) to reconcile the numismatic and radiocarbon calendars.

item.title: The Dogs Before the Map — Lawyer's Cave Coastal Alaska Femur, Koster & Stilwell II Intentional Dog Burials (~10,000 BP), Swan Point & Beringian Canids & Pre-Contact Indigenous American Dog Genomes
item.description: Zooarchaeology, radiocarbon reservoir effects, and paleogenomics of early dogs in the Americas: da Silva Coelho et al. (2021) Lawyer's Cave southeast Alaska femur fragment and marine dietary offset, Perri et al.'s directly dated Koster and Stilwell II Illinois dog burials (~10,190-9,630 cal BP), Lanoë et al. (2024) Swan Point subarctic salmon-fed canids, Graf et al. (2026) Beringian base camp, and Ní Leathlobhair et al. (2018) pre-contact American dog clade.

item.title: The Cargo That Had Many Homes — The 14th-Century BCE Uluburun Shipwreck, Cypriot Oxhide Copper Ingots, Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian Tin Isotopes & Egyptian Cobalt-Blue Glass Cakes
item.description: Provenance chemistry of the Late Bronze Age Uluburun shipwreck (~1320 BCE): Cypriot lead-isotope signatures in 354 oxhide copper ingots, Egyptian trace-element fingerprints in 175 raw glass ingots, and the geochemical debate (Powell et al. 2022 vs. Berger et al. 2023) over Central Asian Mushiston vs. Anatolian tin isotopes and anthropogenic lead contamination.

item.title: The Canoes Under the Lake — Neolithic La Marmotta Submerged Dugouts, Transverse Hull Ribs, Mysterious T-Shaped Rigging Toggles & Prehistoric Mediterranean Crossings
item.description: Archaeological and nautical analysis of the five Early Neolithic dugout canoes submerged in Lake Bracciano at La Marmotta (Gibaja et al. 2024): deliberate multi-species wood selection (oak, alder, poplar, beech), integral transverse hull ribs, enigmatic T-shaped mortised wooden objects along the gunwale, radiocarbon wiggle-matching, and experimental open-water Mediterranean voyages.

item.title: The Cacao in the Clay — 5,300-Year-Old Upper Amazon Cacao Starch, Theobromine & Ancient DNA at Santa Ana–La Florida (Zarrillo 2018), Honduran Beverage Vessels (Henderson 2007) & Pre-Columbian Dispersal Genomics
item.description: Archaeobotany, chemical residue analysis, and archaeogenomics of early Theobroma cacao: Zarrillo et al.'s (2018) triple-line identification of starch grains, theobromine, and ancient DNA in ~5,300-year-old Mayo-Chinchipe ceramic vessels at Santa Ana–La Florida (Ecuador), Henderson et al.'s (2007) Puerto Escondido Honduran spouted vessels before 1000 BCE, Cornejo et al.'s (2018) Criollo domestication genomics, and Lanaud et al.'s (2024) pre-Columbian Ceramic residue dispersal survey.

item.title: The Family Beneath the Long Barrow — Early Neolithic Chambered Tomb Pedigrees, Five-Generation Kinship & Ancient DNA at Hazleton North
item.description: High-resolution ancient DNA kinship reconstruction of 35 individuals from the 5,700-year-old Hazleton North long barrow (Fowler et al. 2021): a five-generation extended family pedigree, patrilineal continuity, four reproductive women with shared male partners, and spatial mapping across north and south L-shaped chambers.

item.title: The Cheese That Kept a History — 3,500-Year-Old Xiaohe Kefir Dairy Proteomics, Ancient Lactobacillus Genomes, Dental Calculus Milk Peptides & Microbial Niche Partitioning
item.description: Biomolecular archaeology and microbial ecology of Bronze Age fermented dairy from the Tarim Basin: LC-MS/MS proteomics of Xiaohe tomb dairy lumps (Yang et al. 2014), dental calculus milk peptides in seven Xiaohe individuals despite lactase non-persistence genotypes (Zhang et al. 2021), ancient DNA capture and phylogeny of 3,500-year-old Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens strains (Liu et al. 2024), and experimental metabolic cross-feeding in modern kefir communities (Blasche et al. 2021).

item.title: The Inheritance in Thin Air — 5,100-Year-Old Zongri Genomes, Denisovan EPAS1 Introgression, Hypoxia Enhancer ENH5 Editing & Endothelial Adaptation
item.description: Evolutionary genomics and functional regulatory biology of high-altitude adaptation on the Tibetan Plateau: 89 ancient genomes spanning 5,100 years beginning at Zongri (Wang et al. 2023), Denisovan-like EPAS1 haplotype introgression and selection timing (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014; Zhang et al. 2021), hypoxia-responsive ENH5 enhancer reporter and deletion experiments (Gray et al. 2022), and iPSC-derived endothelial transcriptomics under hypoxia (Gray et al. 2025).

item.title: The Tree That Stayed in the Timber — Forensic Timber STR & Chloroplast Profiling, Koompassia Log-to-Stump Matching, Shorea Databases & UNODC Likelihood Ratios
item.description: Forensic botany and timber DNA identification: matching three seized Koompassia malaccensis logs (L75, L79, L80) to stump S12 across a 1,465-tree Malaysian reference database (Lee et al. 2025), Shorea leprosula population (45.9%) vs. regional (88.7%) self-assignment across 1,410 trees (Ng et al. 2022), chloroplast vs. nuclear STR inheritance (Ng et al. 2017), Eucalyptus DNA and dendrochronological exclusion (Roman et al. 2020), and UNODC (2016) likelihood-ratio principles.

item.title: The Tooth on Both Sides of the Curve — Bomb-Pulse 14C Enamel Dating, Two-Tooth Developmental Ordering, Bone vs. Hair Turnover Clocks & Cold-Case Identification
item.description: Forensic bomb-pulse radiocarbon (14C) dating and multi-tissue chronology: resolving rising vs. falling bomb-pulse curve intersections using two developing teeth in Speller et al. (2012), enamel AMS preparation and developmental offsets (Buchholz & Spalding 2010), dental collagen vs. vertebral bone turnover vs. hair shaft growth clocks (Bertrand et al. 2024), and the 9-case verified crown-date validation subset (Teglind et al. 2021).

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
item.description: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

item.title: The Floor That Kept the Dead — Neolithic Çatalhöyük Subfloor Burials (Haddow 2025), Shifting Intra-Building Genetic Kinship Across 1,000 Years (63% to 22%, Yaka 2021 & Yüncü 2025) & Maternal Lineage Ties
item.description: Stratigraphic bioarchaeology and ancient DNA of subfloor house burials across Neolithic Anatolia: Haddow et al.'s (2025) house-life-cycle burial patterns at Çatalhöyük (including Building 42's foundation burial), Yaka et al.'s (2021) transition from biological kin burials at Aşıklı Höyük/Boncuklu to co-burial of unrelated individuals, and Yüncü et al.'s (2025) 131-genome time series revealing declining intra-building genetic kinship (63% -> 30% -> 22%), maternal house linkages, and female subadult grave goods.

item.title: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
item.description: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

item.title: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
item.description: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

item.title: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
item.description: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

item.title: The First Anatomists of Speech — 430,000-Yr Ear Bones, Neanderthal Hyoids & Shanidar Care
item.description: Reconstructs Middle Pleistocene speech acoustics from Sima de los Huesos ossicles (2–4 kHz), Kebara 2's hyoid, FOXP2, and Shanidar 1's decades of social survival.

item.title: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
item.description: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

item.title: Wine-Dark Seas & Unspeakable Odors — How Language Shapes Color, Smell & Bedside Pain
item.description: From Gladstone's 1858 shock over Homer's color words and Berlin & Kay's hierarchy to Jahai abstract odor vocabulary and cross-cultural bedside pain ideophones.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

item.title: Twenty-Seven Body Parts to Apothecary Grains — How Language Built Number & Dosing
item.description: Traces embodied human numeracy from Oksapmin 27-locus body counting and Paleolithic bone tallies to Sumerian bullae and life-or-death ancient apothecary metrology.

item.title: Julian Jaynes on Trial — Did Bronze Age Humans Hear Gods Before Inventing 'I'?
item.description: Puts Julian Jaynes's 1976 Bicameral Mind hypothesis on philological and neurobiological trial against Homeric Greek, Middle Kingdom papyri, and corollary-discharge fMRI.

item.title: Diagnosing the Dead — Can Ancient DNA & Modern Medicine Decode Cuneiform & Athens?
item.description: Stages the fierce debate between dental-pulp ancient DNA paleogenomics and medical historians warning against retrospective diagnostic anachronism.

item.title: The Feed That Changed the Carcass — Swine Ractopamine Stereoisomers at Porcine β1/β2-AR, Dietary Lysine Nitrogen-Retention Factorial Trials, AOAC Tissue LC-MS/MS (m/z 302.1→164.1) & Codex vs. FDA vs. EU Frameworks
item.description: Comparative pharmacology, swine nutrition, and food-residue analytics of ractopamine: Andretta's 3,786-pig meta-analysis, RR/RS/SR/SS stereoisomer selectivity at cloned porcine beta1/beta2 adrenoceptors (Mills 2003) vs. human beta2AR structures (4LDO/3SN6), Ross & Pérez lysine-ractopamine interactions vs. Tous drug-free rations, AOAC 2011.23 parent vs. hydrolyzed LC-MS/MS, pig transport heart rate, and JECFA/FDA/Codex/EFSA regulatory splits.

item.title: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT
item.description: Bioarchaeological and analytical investigation of prehistoric dentistry: concentric flint drill striations in Neolithic Mehrgarh molars (Coppa et al. 2006), Upper Paleolithic Villabruna and Riparo Fredian cavities, and synchrotron FTIR/radiocarbon verification of the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling (Bernardini et al. 2012).

item.title: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
item.description: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

item.title: The Tooth That Kept the Tool Marks — Neanderthal Molar Grooves, Villabruna Caries Scraping, Mehrgarh Bow-Drills & Lonche Beeswax
item.description: Scanning electron microscopy, micro-CT, and FTIR spectroscopy of prehistoric worked teeth: Neanderthal interproximal toothpick grooves, Upper Paleolithic Villabruna carious lesion scraping, Neolithic Mehrgarh flint bow-drilled molars, and the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling.

item.title: The Last Meal in the Bog — Tollund Man's Gut Contents, Barley-Flax-Weed Gruel, Whipworm Eggs & Forensic Reconstruction
item.description: Multi-proxy forensic re-analysis of Tollund Man's large-intestinal contents (Nielsen et al. 2021): plant macrofossils, pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, ancient DNA, proteins, lipids, Trichuris trichiura eggs, and why threshing waste was intentionally added.

item.title: The Seasons Inside a Tooth — Neanderthal Enamel Retzius Lines, Oxygen Isotopes, Barium Nursing Traces & Lead Bands
item.description: High-resolution laser-ablation and SHRIMP microprobe reading of Neanderthal teeth (Smith et al. 2018): daily enamel cross-striations, seasonal oxygen-18 cycles, barium/calcium nursing transitions, and acute wintertime lead exposure bands.

item.title: What Pathogen DNA Can Date — Ancient Treponemal Genomes, Radiocarbon Calibration & Molecular Clock Boundaries
item.description: Paleogenomic investigation of pre-Columbian Treponema pallidum and ancient pathogens (Majander et al. 2024; Barquera et al. 2025; 5,500-year-old Sabana de Bogota genome): damage patterns, radiocarbon priors, recombination filtration, and tip-dating limits.

item.title: Evolved for the Impossible — Bajau 13-Min Divers, Denisovan Sherpas & 13.7 °C Survival
item.description: How genetic evolution (Bajau PDE10A giant spleens, Denisovan Sherpa EPAS1) and Q10 thermodynamics (Anna Bågenholm's 13.7 °C resuscitation) shield the 20W human brain.
